hints.title: Generating All Platform and Experiment Pairs
hints.text: The platforms are Android, iOS, Web and experiment types are Reading, Sports, Programming. Every one of the 9 combinations must appear in the output.

hints.title: Cartesian Product of Categories
hints.text: Create a cross join of the three platforms and three experiment names to generate all 9 combinations.

hints.title: Joining and Counting
hints.text: Left join the combinations with Experiments on platform and experiment_name, then count experiment_id grouped by platform and experiment_name.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH Platforms AS (
    SELECT 'Android' AS platform
    UNION ALL SELECT 'IOS'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Web'
),
Names AS (
    SELECT 'Reading' AS experiment_name
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Sports'
    UNION ALL SELECT 'Programming'
),
AllPairs AS (
    SELECT p.platform, n.experiment_name
    FROM Platforms p
    CROSS JOIN Names n
)
SELECT
    a.platform,
    a.experiment_name,
    COUNT(e.experiment_id) AS num_experiments
FROM AllPairs a
LEFT JOIN Experiments e
    ON a.platform = e.platform
    AND a.experiment_name = e.experiment_name
GROUP BY a.platform, a.experiment_name;
```

complexity.time: O(E) where E is number of experiments conducted
complexity.space: O(1) output fixed at exactly 9 rows
variables: E: number of records in Experiments table
complexity.notes: Cross join of dimensions left joined with facts table.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Grouping on the Experiments table alone drops combinations that have 0 trials.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dimension cross join ensures zero-count combinations are retained.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should construct Cartesian product and use COUNT(column) instead of COUNT(*).

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def count_experiments(experiments: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    platforms = pd.DataFrame({'platform': ['Android', 'IOS', 'Web']})
    names = pd.DataFrame({'experiment_name': ['Reading', 'Sports', 'Programming']})
    grid = platforms.merge(names, how='cross')
    counts = experiments.groupby(['platform', 'experiment_name'])['experiment_id'].count().reset_index(name='num_experiments')
    res = grid.merge(counts, on=['platform', 'experiment_name'], how='left')
    res['num_experiments'] = res['num_experiments'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return res
solutions.approach: Cartesian grid cross merge with counts in pandas
